exposure: Postnatal diagnosis of critical congenital heart disease (CHD)
Prenatal diagnosis of critical congenital heart disease (CHD)
cohort: 296 maternal-neonatal pairs with a diagnosis of complex CHD (186 prenatal diagnoses, 110 postnatal diagnoses) from 2011 to 2013
finding: Prenatal diagnosis of critical congenital heart disease was associated with earlier gestational age at delivery, lower birth weight, and a higher likelihood of cesarean delivery compared to postnatal diagnosis.
mod_finding: Neonates with cesarean delivery trended toward a longer length of stay (2.6 days longer) and were born earlier compared to other delivery modalities.
